decisions.decision: Version input data and code for reproducible weekly forecasts
decisions.context: Forecasts must be reproducible for any past week, so each run needs traceable inputs and implementation. The brief does not prescribe a storage or versioning technology.

alternatives.label: Record immutable data snapshots and code versions per run

chosen.label: Record immutable data snapshots and code versions per run

decisions.rationale: This directly supports replaying a past week with its original inputs and code. The additional storage and versioning work fits a small team better than relying on mutable sources.
consequences: Each run records data and code versions.
Historical snapshots require retention and storage.

decisions.decision: Separate model experiments from the weekly production run
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly without breaking the weekly run. A three-person team also needs a small, understandable path from experimentation to production.

alternatives.label: Promote candidates through an isolated evaluation step

chosen.label: Promote candidates through an isolated evaluation step

decisions.rationale: An evaluation step allows the team to try candidates independently and promote only a selected model. This balances iteration speed with continuity of the weekly forecast.
consequences: Candidate and production models need distinct versions.
Promotion adds an explicit workflow step.

decisions.decision: Make the weekly forecast pipeline a single team-owned workflow
decisions.context: The team of three data scientists owns the pipeline end to end, and forecasts are produced weekly. The brief favors a manageable operational shape but does not specify a platform.

alternatives.label: Use one scheduled workflow for data, training, and forecasts
Split work across independently operated services

chosen.label: Use one scheduled workflow for data, training, and forecasts

decisions.rationale: A single workflow keeps ownership and run status clear for a small team. It can be decomposed later if scale or operational needs justify the added service boundaries.
consequences: The workflow needs clear stages and failure reporting.
One team remains responsible for the full run.

uncovered: Forecast horizon and required output schema
